headline: Rain and gusty winds arrive tonight, then a cooler weekend with possible first frost.
summary: A cold front sweeps through western Washington overnight, followed by noticeably cooler air. Behind it, showers linger in the mountains and over the central Sound on Friday, with light rain totals. Winds pick up early Friday and peak through the early afternoon, with gusts of 20 to 30 mph widely and strong gusts likely in the Strait of Juan de Fuca and on Whidbey Island. Winds ease Friday evening. A weak disturbance brings a few light showers Saturday. Cascade valleys could touch freezing Sunday morning, the first frost concern of the season, though that is uncertain and depends on clearing skies and fog. Drier, cool weather follows early next week, with another system bringing rain and breezy winds Tuesday into Wednesday.
